definitions.gloss: to hold out, to endure, to withstand
definitions.explanation: To continue to resist or survive under difficult conditions; to hang on despite hardship.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}はなんとか{不況|ふきょう}を{持|も}ち{堪|こた}えた。
examples.english: The company somehow managed to hold out through the recession.

examples.japanese: {堤防|ていぼう}が{洪水|こうずい}に{持|も}ち{堪|こた}えるか{心配|しんぱい}だ。
examples.english: I'm worried whether the levee will hold against the flood.

examples.japanese: あと{少|すこ}し{持|も}ち{堪|こた}えれば、{救援|きゅうえん}が{来|く}る。
examples.english: If we can just hold out a little longer, help will arrive.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {自動詞|じどうし} (intransitive).

COMPOUND VERB: Formed from {持|も}つ (to hold) + {堪|こた}える (to endure). The combination emphasizes sustained endurance or resistance.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{不況|ふきょう}を{持|も}ち{堪|こた}える (weather a recession)
・{攻撃|こうげき}に{持|も}ち{堪|こた}える (withstand an attack)
・{困難|こんなん}に{持|も}ち{堪|こた}える (endure hardships)
・なんとか{持|も}ち{堪|こた}える (somehow hold out)

SIMILAR WORDS: {耐|た}える emphasizes bearing pain or difficulty; {持|も}ち{堪|こた}える emphasizes maintaining a position or continuing to function.
